messages:
maria: Heads-up — HPA scaled the `frontend` deployment to 8 replicas based on our p50 latency custom metric, but we still have 6 pods in Pending state.
maria: kubectl get pods -n prod | grep frontend
```
frontend-5f9d6   0/1   Pending   0     2m
frontend-5f9d6   0/1   Pending   0     2m
frontend-5f9d6   0/1   Pending   0     2m
...
```
maria: Describe shows: "0/1 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu." — looks like CA didn't create GPU nodes for the gpu-node-pool.
aj: Can you paste `kubectl describe hpa frontend -n prod` and `kubectl get events -n prod --sort-by='.lastTimestamp'`?
maria: HPA snippet:
```
Name: frontend
Metrics: external/trace_latency_ms (target 200ms) on pods  -> current value 260ms
Replicas: 2 -> 8 (increase)
Conditions: able to scale: true
```

maria: Events:
```
FailedScheduling   2m  default-scheduler  0/1 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu
Warning  TriggeredScaleUp  2m  autoscaler-controller  Scale-up for node group gpu-pool failed: autoscaling disabled (annotation: cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/scale-down-disabled=true)
```
autoscaler-bot: Note: nodegroup `gpu-pool` has autoscaling disabled via annotation `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/scale-down-disabled=true` (set by infra during maintenance window)
aj: Ah — autoscaler disabled on that nodegroup. That explains why CA didn't create nodes even though pods requested GPUs.
kevin: Also double-check pod tolerations/affinity — if pods require `nodeAffinity: gpu=true` but the nodegroup label is `accelerator: nvidia-tesla-t4` CA may still be able to scale but pods won't schedule if labels/taints don't match.
maria: Deployment spec has `nodeSelector: { cloud.google.com/gke-accelerator: nvidia-tesla-t4 }` but gpu-pool nodes are labeled `accelerator=nvidia-tesla-t4` (missing the cloud.google.com key). That mismatch will block scheduling even if CA could add nodes.
jyoti: And remember our Prometheus adapter mapping for the latency metric was changed last week. HPA was pointed at `external/trace_latency_ms` but adapter exposes `requests_latency_seconds_bucket` under `custom.metrics.k8s.io`. If HPA and adapter names don't align CA/HPA interplay becomes noisy.
aj: Can you run `kubectl get --raw "/apis/custom.metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1/namespaces/prod/services/frontend:requests_latency_seconds"` to confirm? If it 404s, HPA might be reading fallback metric and overreacting.
maria: Ran that, got 404. Adapter logs show: "mapping missing for metric 'trace_latency_ms' -> metric not found".
kevin: Root causes we should fix:
- Re-enable autoscaling for gpu-pool or create a dedicated burstable GPU group
- Standardize labels between nodepool and pod nodeSelector (or switch to nodeAffinity)
- Fix Prometheus adapter metric name mapping so HPA reads the intended latency metric
- Consider a warm-pool of 1-2 GPU nodes to handle sudden spikes (cost vs latency tradeoff)

jyoti: +1 on warm pool. Cold-adding GPUs takes ~4-6 minutes which kills p50/p95 for gamified workloads.
aj: Cost note: Warm pool of 2 T4s in us-central1 is ~$0.6/hr => ~$432/month; cheaper than recurring SLO miss penalties for product
kevin: Also consider using a node group with autoscaler scale-up-only for burst (disable scale-down) and rely on Dedicated for baseline traffic.
sre-bot: FYI: GCP GPU quota in us-central1 currently at 12 GPUs used 12/12 (quota exhausted). Any new scale-ups will be throttled until quota increased or alternative region used.
maria: Good catch — our quota is saturated, CA would still fail. Next steps I'm going to:
- Open a GCP quota request for +10 GPUs in us-central1 (assigned to me)
- Temporarily re-enable autoscaler on gpu-pool during business hours (kevin)
- Patch deployment to use `accelerator=nvidia-tesla-t4` label (aj)
- Update Prometheus adapter mapping for `trace_latency_ms` -> (jyoti)

kevin: I'll also propose a short-term policy: reserve 1 GPU in Dedicated for baseline, plus 1 warm spare in the burst pool. We can re-evaluate after two weeks.
maria: Thanks — I'll create a short runbook for this incident and link to the quota request + PRs.
aj: If anyone wants to test locally, here's a quick debug command to simulate Pending pods: `kubectl run tmp --image=nginx --requests='limits.memory=2Gi, limits.nvidia.com/gpu=1' --restart=Never` will reproduce scheduling failure.
jyoti: I'll test the adapter mapping change in staging and ping here when done.
kevin: Assigning follow-ups: @maria -> quota + runbook, @aj -> deployment label patch, @jyoti -> adapter mapping change, @kevin -> GPU warm-pool proposal.
maria: Cool. I'll update this thread as things progress. :thumbsup:
